limitations: All main text, methods, references, ten main/extended figures and two clinical tables read. All cells of TablesS1/S2 read, but their native page pixels pending. All six source-blot PDF pages inspected, four distinct imagepages; F4/FS1 byte-identical rendered duplicates of F2p3/p4. Raw sequencing/flow files not read or reanalysed; no independent laboratory replication.

Five unrelated patients with four heterozygous variants and CID, four with ED and two neuropathy. P5 donor father unavailable: de novo not proven despite abstract generalisation; P1–4 parents tested. GEL selection explicitly filters for IEI/ED and recurrence, so not unbiased penetrance evidence. Four HCT outcomes improve immune function observationally; no proof of correction of ectodermal/neuropathy manifestations or comparative treatment efficacy.

Normal ITPR3 expression in LCL/fibroblast and heterologous transfectants does not establish normal channel function. Primary T-cell protein unmeasured because lymphopenia. KO alone preserves SOCE; reexpression of A196T/I2506N/R2524C disrupts it, supporting active dominant interference over haploinsufficiency. Engineered KO/reconstitution retains ITPR1/2, is not exact native heterozygous stoichiometry, and uses clones from one KO parent. R2524H not directly reconstituted: R2524C at same residue used as proxy. ER-leak mechanism inferred rather than measured as single-channel gating of every allele.

Cell-context differences matter: T-cell responses impaired while fibroblast ATP response not significantly different. Ionomycin rescues acute Ca influx; not a clinical treatment. No constitutive SOCE shown. Abundance/localisation and structural delta-deltaG predictions are not functional equivalence. Source blots show variable exposures and truncated/lower bands; no independent densitometry performed.

Human T-cell RNAseq Methods explicitly says reads aligned to mouse mm10. This is a material unresolved methods discrepancy, possibly textual error; no raw alignment audit or author contact performed. RNA signatures cannot be treated as independently reproduced. Metabolic-marker protein changes are not direct flux measurements. RNA IL2/IFNG differences coexist with normal tested cytokine production/degranulation. Memory skew, small patient numbers and nested technical repetitions limit inference. Figure5 statistical caption mixes Mann–Whitney with all-statistics bilateral t-tests.

Patient HSPC thymopoiesis experiments use marrow versus healthy cord blood, creating source/age confounding; demonstrate late differentiation block in two cases, not absence of all thymopoiesis. HCT results are time-dependent. P1 clinical HCT age9 vs Table2 age24/14years post implies age10; P2 narrative age3 vs age6/2years post implies4. Do not silently harmonise.

Clinical table conflicts retained: P2 Table1 B-cell lymphopenia No but Table2 280/µl below896–2316; P1 narrative mildly low Bcells but Table2 normal260 and Table1No. P3 lowTRECs7797 below10th8538; source narrative also low, so packetnegative is wrong. P3 microdontia positive inTable1/narrative but packetnegative. P5 hypohidrosis narrativeYes versusTable1No. Atrialseptaldefect is P4, not P2, confirmed tablepixels.

P1/P2 both female by narrative and Fig1 circles; packets incorrectly male. P2 lower-incisor morphology does not support maxillary lateral incisor term. Table2 absolute T-cell counts cannot automatically establish proportions: P1 CD8/CD3=120/170~71%, P2~43%, P3~30%; low absolute numbers do not show low CD8 fraction. Naive-CD8 counts P1/P3 similarly not a proven proportional decrease. P2 proportional naive reduction directly visibleFig5/S1.

Main variant transcript NM_002224.3 versus packets .4; same reported coding/protein and GRCh38 genomic loci, but version equivalence not independently remapped. P2 common maternal R1850Q (8.2%,6079gnomADhom) unphased with I2506N, so not a demonstrated recessive pair. Figure2B P3 label c7517G>A appears transposed versus c7571G>A Table1/Fig1/text; exact allele anchored by concordant genomic and protein description.
